item.title: Microsoft plans to offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers as part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce as it invests heavily in AI. That amounts to just over a quarter of its total staff.
item.description:
Microsoft plans to offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers as part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce as it invests heavily in AI. That amounts to just over a quarter of its total staff.
Select personnel in the U.S., Canada, the UK, and India at the vice president level and below will be eligible for a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO), Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, said in a note to staff today. Microsoft had 223,000 employees as of the end of June, a number that was down from 228,000 at the end of 2025.
According to Bloomberg, the cuts come amid a focus on AI, with costly data centers supplying cloud services to the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI. In June, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella addressed community backlash to the company's massive AI data center buildout, which has sparked concern over power costs, environmental concerns, and the potential impact on jobs. He insisted one of Microsoft's data centers' daily water usage over the course of an entire year is roughly equivalent to what a single restaurant would use. Some staff at Microsoft, including those working on data centers, are excluded from the buyout offer.
Every Video Game Franchise Xbox Owns After Acquiring Activision Blizzard
According to CNBC, employees have until December to decide whether they will take the offer, and those who do will leave Microsoft on December 31.
The buyout offer comes just three months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 roles, or what was about 2.1% of its global workforce. The Xbox layoffs, which hit 1,600 staff in July as part of Asha Sharma's "reset" of the gaming business, formed a part of those cuts. Earlier this month, an Xbox business strategist claimed that everyone in the video games industry was using AI while pretending not to.
And earlier this year, more than 30% of eligible employees chose to to take Microsoft's first ever voluntary retirement program.
Photo by Oliver Berg/picture alliance via Getty Images.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.
item.description:
Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.
Aftermath reported that the studio let 26 employees go, just weeks after Ghost of Yotei's DLC and Complete Edition were released on PS5. The studio has roughly 200 employees as it stands. Aftermath shared an email that was sent out to the team from studio leadership, which reveals that "challenges in the market" and changes in the scope of the team for its next project were the deciding factors in the layoffs.
“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result," the email reads.
Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Screenshots
The note also stated that they will discuss the plans for the studio's future next week.
”We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can. … There's no getting around that this is a hard day. Next week we will go into more details about the future.”
As of right now, it's unclear what Sucker Punch's next game will be; it does sound like there is another project in the cards based on the studio's statement. Some want a return to Infamous, whether through a collection of remasters/remakes or a brand-new entry. Others want a new Sly Cooper. And of course, there's appetite for more games in the studio's Ghost series. It wouldn't be surprising if at least one of these happens, as new IP with a big AAA budget is becoming harder and harder to justify.
Ghost of Yotei was one of the biggest games of fall 2025, selling 3.3 million copies in its first month. It's also one of the best-reviewed PS5 exclusives to date. It was also expected to come to PC at some point, but unfortunately, that plan was scrapped when Sony opted to move away from PC. The game recently got a Complete Edition, which added a brand-new story DLC and other additional content. It's unclear if this moved any significant copies or if the audience for the game already capped out with its initial release.
The layoffs also come during a tumultuous time for PlayStation, which has been upsetting fans over its controversial shift to an all-digital future starting in 2028. The company will phase out physical copies of games in favor of digital releases, likely beginning with PS6. PlayStation also shuttered Bluepoint, a beloved studio that was best known for high-quality remasters, ports, and remakes such as Demon's Souls for PS5. Additionally, PlayStation attempted to scrap development on Hideo Kojima's next gen game, Physint, until Microsoft swooped in to save it.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on the original Star Trek series, has died at age 90. Koenig joined the NBC series Star Trek in its second season as Russian crewmember Ensign Pavel Andreievich Chekov.
item.description:
Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on the original Star Trek series, has died at age 90.
“The late actor's rep tells us ... Walter's daughter, Danielle, and his niece were by his side when he died of old age at his home in North Hollywood on Sunday,” TMZ reports.
Koenig joined the NBC series Star Trek in its second season as the USS Enterprise’s Russian crewmember Ensign Pavel Andreievich Chekov. With his Beatles-style mop of hair, the boyish Chekov was meant to appeal to younger viewers a la Davy Jones of The Monkees.
As Chekov, Koenig would appear in the latter two seasons of the original series and then in all six feature films featuring the cast.
With Koenig’s death, only William Shatner (Captain Kirk) and George Takei (Mr. Sulu) remain alive from the original cast.
Takei took to social media to salute his longtime co-star:
Marvin Walter Koenig was born in Chicago on Sept. 14, 1936. The Hollywood Reporter recounts that he studied at Neighborhood Playhouse in New York alongside future sci-fi and comedy icon Christopher Lloyd, who would star opposite Koenig in Star Trek III: The Search for Spock.
After Star Trek was canceled – and the character of Chekov was left out of the animated series – Koenig turned to writing episodic television series.
Following Star Trek, Koenig returned to the sci-fi genre with his role as Alfred Bester on Babylon 5. In 2017, Koenig reprised the role of Chekov (as “The Admiral”) for the crowdsourced online series Renegades.
Koenig was widowed in 2022 after the death of his wife Judy. His son, Growing Pains actor Andrew Koenig, committed suicide in 2010.
You can read our archival interview with the Trek legend from 2024 where he looked back on the good, the bad, and the hilarious after 57 years of the franchise.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Sony may have exclusive access to AMD's next-generation graphics architecture for a potential PlayStation handheld, the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said.
item.description:
Sony may have exclusive access to AMD's next-generation graphics architecture for a potential PlayStation handheld, the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said.
There have been rumors of a next-generation PlayStation handheld for some time now, after the success of the Nintendo Switch and a wide gamut of PC gaming handhelds. Indeed, in June, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hideaki Nishino suggested PlayStation may move towards more hybrid, Switch-like consoles in the future to match modern on-the-go players.
When I watched the latest Patreon-exclusive DF Direct, Digital Foundry's Richard Leadbetter claimed that "there's been some behind-the-scenes discussion that Sony has an exclusive of sorts with AMD for RDNA 5 for handheld," and that the only other, presumably handheld, chip he knows of in production at AMD is what's going to be known as Z3, which is unlikely to have RDNA 5 graphics.
The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time
AMD and Sony have been working closely for the last couple of years, teaming up on an initiative called 'Project Amethyst,' which ultimately resulted in both PSSR 2 on the PS5 Pro and FSR 4.1 for PC and Xbox.
Speaking of Xbox, it sounds like Microsoft has handheld gaming plans of its own. Project Helix will include a whole range of devices, we were recently told, and a handheld will reportedly be the first out the gate. Fortune recently reported that Microsoft plans to release a handheld by holiday 2027, with the next-gen console following in 2028. The chips going into either of these platforms hasn't been confirmed, but AMD did come out and tease that FSR Diamond would be launching with Project Helix – of which the handheld is a part of – and that would likely be running on RDNA 5.
AMD would have reason to supercharge its handheld chip offerings for a wide range of devices, as well. Intel's Panther Lake handheld chip launched at Computex 2026 and, at least in my testing, absolutely bodies the AMD Ryzen Z2 Extreme. The Z2 Extreme only uses an RDNA 3.5 GPU, which was already an older architecture when it launched last year. The Intel Arc G3, on the other hand, uses the same GPU that powers its latest laptops, just with a few of the CPU cores disabled.
With how expensive handhelds have become lately, the whole category is in danger of vanishing until the RAM crisis abates, and so it's possible that Sony's handheld is the only one that springs for the added cost of RDNA 5. But, unless Sony inks some kind of exclusive deal with AMD, I am sure other devices using RDNA 5 will exist eventually – maybe even Xbox's own first-party handheld.
This isn’t the first PlayStation handheld tease, either. Last year, Moore’s Law Is Dead reported on an unannounced PS6 handheld that would be dockable and backwards compatible with PS4 and PS5 games. There was also a brief mention of what was described as a PS6 S, which sounded like it could be to the PS6 what the Xbox Series S is to the Xbox Series X. If true, you’d assume it would be a cheaper option.
Are you interested in handheld options for next-gen PlayStation and Xbox consoles?

item.title: If you've ever wondered what a fusion of Vampire Survivors and Heroes of Might and Magic would look like, then Heroes Never Die might be the game for you. It's a newly announced fantasy strategy game from developer Ludogram that "aims to take the best of the survival formula and fuse it with more tactical decisions, real-time army building, and powerful fantasy heroes." It will be released in 2027 for PC.
item.description:
If you've ever wondered what a fusion of Vampire Survivors and Heroes of Might and Magic would look like, then Heroes Never Die might be the game for you. It's a newly announced fantasy strategy game from developer Ludogram that "aims to take the best of the survival formula and fuse it with more tactical decisions, real-time army building, and powerful fantasy heroes." It will be released in 2027 for PC.
In Heroes Never Die, you'll choose your titular hero – there are over 20 in the lineup – and battle not just monster hordes but also rival heroes. Each hero has their own skills, but no matter who you pick, you'll seek to upgrade your town by gathering resources and fighting foes. There are also four factions and over 60 different units, with the developers promising that no two runs will be alike.
Heroes Never Die Screenshots
“We’re delighted to finally announce Heroes Never Die, a project we’ve been working on in the shadows for a couple of years”, said creative director Edouard Gaudel. “We cannot wait to see our first players fighting hordes of monsters, and evolving their armies while meeting our heroes. Don’t forget to join our upcoming Playtest!”
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: A hacker sparked an uproar within the PlayStation 5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.
item.description:
A hacker sparked an uproar within the PlayStation 5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.
A hacker who goes by the handle “Jordy” was awarded the bounty from Sony for reporting a vulnerability — found using AI — on the PS5 console. The bug was reported to HackerOne, a site that works with companies to plug issues in their products and services. Essentially, Sony pays hackers to find exploits, then pays them money not to release them until the security hole has been patched.
There wouldn’t normally be anything particularly unusual about a hack being reported to Sony — but in the case of this PS5 exploit, a prominent security engineer discovered it months ago but wanted to hold onto it until GTA 6 launched. Then Jordy discovered it with AI and reported it, triggering the controversy.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
The exploit in question is a ‘Hypervisor Bug’ that affects the PS5 on firmware from 13.60 up to 14.00. A hypervisor bug is a fault inside the core software or firmware layer, which allows hackers to execute kernel code to, for example, boot Linux on a machine not designed to do it.
You might have seen a spate of headlines about how AI has fueled an explosion of hacks across the internet. Information security experts are calling this month ‘Black October’ due to several major security incidents and vulnerability disclosures prompted by the growing use of artificial intelligence in research.
Google security engineer Andy Nguyen, aka theflow0, had been working on getting Linux running on PS5 for months. Indeed, back in March, theflow0 showcased the results of his work. But Jordy’s AI-powered bug report put an end to that work. “I am stepping away from the PS5 scene and stopping all my work on PS5 Linux,” he said. “After pouring my heart and months of my life into it, including plans to finish PS5 Pro support and release in 2027, it's all down the sink.
“The scene used to be a group of highly talented researchers, but now it is just a bunch of noobs using LLMs and writing hacks they don't even understand. Slop kiddies found the only hypervisor bug left, which I had also found a while ago, and decided to report to Sony.”
In a conversation with IGN, Jordy admitted using generative AI to find the bug that netted him $50,000. He claimed that theflow0 found the bug back in 2025 but had kept it secret. When Jordy announced he’d found a hypervisor bug himself, theflow0 reached out to see if it was the same one he found the year before. Jordy and theflow0 initially agreed to not report the bug to HackerOne, but another researcher quickly found the same bug shortly after. Jordy made the decision to report the bug as other researchers stumbled on it by using generative AI, closing the window to claim the bounty from Sony.
“I decided I would report it,” Jordy said. “If I and another person can find it with LLM, so can someone else.”
theflow0 couldn’t be reached for comment.
It’s not just the use of AI that made Jordy’s bounty claim controversial. Players who wanted to boot Linux on their consoles are upset because of a certain video game coming out in November. Before the bug was reported, it would have been possible to load Linux onto a PS5 and still run the console through the Sony operating system, which would have allowed people running Linux to play GTA 6 when not using the jailbreak.
“People wanted to buy and play GTA 6 legally on their normal PS5 OS without losing the ability to dual-boot Linux on the same console,” madwax0r, creator of the PS5 emulator tracker and scam blacklist Kaishaku, told IGN. “Think of the PS5 Linux project like turning your console into a high-end Steam Machine that runs off an external USB drive. It's a temporary soft-mod, so whenever you reboot the console, it goes right back to being a normal PS5.
“The catch is that to download and play GTA 6 on November 19, Sony requires you to update to the latest system firmware and sign into PSN. theflow0 wanted researchers to hold off reporting the hypervisor bug until after November 19 so that the launch-day firmware required for GTA 6 would still have the unpatched flaw baked in. That way, players could update their PS5 on launch day, buy GTA 6 legally, and still use the exploit to boot Linux on the same machine.”
Presumably, some would have used the exploit for more nefarious means. There’s sentiment on the internet that Sony “deserved this” because of its policy to end physical discs by 2028. Pirating games — including GTA 6 — is a distinct possibility as those in the homebrew scene continue to point AI at the inner workings of the PS5, with Sony battling to keep up with each potential jailbreak by issuing fresh firmware updates.
Because Jordy — whose mother is terminally ill — reported the bug early, Sony had the chance to patch the exploit ahead of GTA 6’s launch. This leaves modders who want to run Linux stuck with a choice: keep their PS5 offline to run Linux, or update and make the console GTA 6-ready while locking themselves out of Linux.
“What really poured fuel on the fire is the AI angle,” said madwax0r. “Historically, hypervisor bugs were so rare that a researcher could quietly sit on one for a year. Now, with people running console code through LLMs (large language models) to hunt for flaws, multiple people are stumbling onto the same bugs at the same time. Theflow wanted to hold the bug for the community, while Jordy — seeing a third hacker also find it with AI tools, and facing heavy personal pressure with his mother's terminal illness — took the guaranteed $50,000 payout before someone else beat him to it.”
Part of the reason Jordy’s bounty claim went viral was because of his tweet announcing the win. “I can at least buy GTA with this I think,” he said on Twitter, along with a screenshot of the payout. At the time of writing, the tweet had 1.8 million views. IGN asked Jordy if he thought the tweet might have been what antagonized the audience. “Probably but that was the point,” he replied. “I’m nearly 30 years old. I could care less about people not being able to pirate a game, let alone do I want to enable modding it.”
Because of the timing of the bounty claim, some of the audience also believe Jordy was coached on how to find the bug by theflow0, which is another reason people are angry. The researcher denies this and claims he found it independently. “Yes, with AI,” he said. “A lot of people want to downplay that but nobody else is finding bugs like that.” Jordy added that theflow0 is “a legend” and a respectable figure in the industry.
Since he announced he had received the $50,000 bounty, Jordy has faced repeated criticism on social media from those in the scene who believe he should have held off. “50k in bank but 0 friends left. Worth it?” one person asked. “You're insane to think I lost friends over reporting a bug I found myself, even flow who isn't happy with my choice I can still contact privately,” Jordy replied. “You guys act like I'm a domestic terrorist or something?”
Some, though, have supported Jordy cashing in on the bounty. “$50k pays the bills, your opinion doesn’t,” one person said in response to a critic. “You also would report bug to get 50k, like that’s a life changing amount of money for a lot of people,” another added. “He got paid 50k$ idiot! What did u think that he was gonna do, turn it down so you could play GTA 6 on a Nintendo DS?” commented another.
The Best PS5 Games
Last week, Sony issued a new PS5 firmware update that some believe was designed to combat the homebrew community's ongoing effort to jailbreak the console. There is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security. This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, which comes out in less than a month, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.
Jordy also claimed that this won’t be the last hypervisor bug people find on PS5. Cybersecurity researcher Eric Parker agreed. “I imagine there will probably be another exploit at some point,” he said. If Jordy’s claims are true, it might not be the last hypervisor bug on PS5, which means hackers could find a way around the 14.00 patch in the future. Linux is already up and running on pre-patch PS5s.
The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.
For Jordy, the money represents time — time he can spend with his family and looking after his sick mother. “I will continue to research,” he said. “Just really no time lately.”
Photo by Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spent the weekend doubling down on his severe criticism of Valve, calling Steam’s AI content disclosure a “political act.”
item.description:
Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spent the weekend doubling down on his severe criticism of Valve, calling Steam’s AI content disclosure a “political act.”
The controversial majority owner of Epic is all in on AI, having recently triggered a “huge pivot” of the company to retool it for “maximum AI acceleration,” Sweeney said. Epic is a long-standing rival of Gabe Newell’s Valve, with the Epic Games Store struggling to make a dent in Steam’s dominance over the PC gaming market even as it offers developers more financially beneficial terms.
Sweeney is particularly upset with Steam’s AI content disclosure policy, which requires developers to disclose the use of AI in “creating content that ships with your game, and is consumed by players.” This includes content such as artwork, sound, narrative, and localization. It does not include “efficiency gains” through the use of AI tools.
On Friday, Sweeney hit out at Valve’s policy, saying “forcing developers to write a political statement to be used against them by the hate mob they’re helping organize is abhorrent.” This statement sparked a backlash online, with a number of people — developers included — confused by the suggestion that an AI disclosure was political in any way, and insisting that Valve was only providing clarity its customers wanted.
“Customers have a right to know what they’re buying,” David Goldfarb, founder of Metal Hellsinger developer The Outsiders and former Battlefield developer, replied. “They still bought Arc Raiders, they will definitely buy games they want to buy, AI use or no. Does it disadvantage small teams who need to leverage AI to survive? Jury’s out. Calling it a hate mob is far-fetched.”
Undeterred, Sweeney issued a number of social media posts defending his position, saying AI disclosures are “just as partisan as mandatory political essays or forcing developers to list their voting history to drive cancel campaigns and public struggle sessions.”
When one person challenged Sweeney on this, accusing him of being "anti-consumer" for forcing something consumers don't like on them, the Fortnite boss compared Steam's AI disclosures to Valve forcing developers to list their political affiliations.
"Say there is a large contingent of gamers that don’t like democrats or, equivalently, republicans. Should Valve force developers to list their political affiliation? Is that pro-consumer? Do you think that policy would have a positive effect on gaming?" he said. As you can imagine, this statement was ridiculed in the replies, with one person saying "equating AI to how a person votes is pure cope gymnastics."
Does AI-Generated Content Bother You In Games?

item.title: Microsoft has said it's exploring the possibility of a company coming in to support Arkane Lyon as it works to finish development of Marvel's Blade, and that it's extending the deadline to find a buyer for the studio.
item.description:
Microsoft has said it's exploring the possibility of a company coming in to support Arkane Lyon as it works to finish development of Marvel's Blade, and that it's extending the deadline to find a buyer for the studio.
Arkane Lyon's 217 employees are currently at risk of losing their jobs unless a buyer is found for the famed immersive sim studio. According to a recent report, Microsoft wanted to close the studio as part of its sweeping cuts in the summer, but French law prevented it from doing so straight away.
Following that report, which claimed Arkane had until November 13 to find a new owner, Microsoft has extended the deadline by a month. Additionally, it said it's looking for a partner to "support" Arkane, presumably with financing, for the final stretch of Marvel’s Blade's development.
Who Is Blade? Marvel’s Vampire Hunter Explained
"We have extended the consultation period by one additional month as we explore options, including finding a partner to support the studio through the development work still ahead," a Microsoft representative told PC Gamer. "This is a defined extension, and we remain committed to keeping the Works Council informed throughout the process."
The studio was first informed of Microsoft’s decision on July 16, shortly after new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced similar plans for Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs — Ninja Theory was closed while the other studios went independent. Over 1,600 jobs were cut as part of the layoffs across Microsoft's gaming business. More followed, and more are to come.
Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier said he’d be surprised if Arkane Lyon ends up being shut down, however. “Let me share some positive news for a change,” he said on BlueSky. “Despite all the gloomy headlines today, my understanding is that there are multiple paths actively being explored that would save Arkane Lyon.
“Anything can happen during negotiations, but at this point I'd be surprised if the studio is shut down. One important piece of context that many people might not realize: Shutting down a game studio is expensive. Shutting down a French game studio — thanks to labor laws requiring an extended severance period — is VERY expensive. Xbox doesn't want to take on those costs.”
The union is currently pushing for re-employment of affected staff to other studios within Xbox, should Microsoft fail to secure a deal for Arkane Lyon to survive. "The redundancy plan must be adapted to the video game market where, currently, the prospects for returning to work are extremely limited,” said a union rep.
Negotiations are ongoing, but the union hasn’t ruled out seeing Microsoft in court. "Microsoft is looking to divest itself of Arkane, even though the studio is doing well, in order to save money and improve the profitability of its short-term investments," said the rep.
Marvel’s Blade was on track for a reveal early next year and a release in the fourth quarter of 2027, IGN understands. Blade was announced in December 2023 with a reveal trailer, but we've seen nothing of it since. In June, Bethesda Game Studios head Todd Howard was quoted as saying he'd recently seen what Arkane Lyon was cooking up and was impressed. "I'm not at liberty to say when [we'll see more]," Howard teased at the time, "but I saw some stuff just yesterday [on May 21] and the folks at Arkane [Studios, the developers] are doing a really, really great job."
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Eric Bauza, the voice acting legend behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and countless other classic characters, has died at 46.
item.description:
Eric Bauza, the voice acting legend behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and countless other classic characters, has died at 46.
Confirmation of Bauza's passing arrived in a post shared on his Instagram account. As reported by KTLA, the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner's Office said he died October 25, 2026, of hypertensive cardiovascular disease.
Additional details surrounding the sudden announcement remain unclear. His family promised to share more soon with a message posted on social media.
"Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly," a message from his family said. "More details to come."
Bauza has such a thorough career in animation and voice acting that almost everyone who has enjoyed any TV shows, movies, or games in the last 25 years has probably heard his work. His time lending his unforgettable talent in the industry started with smaller roles in the 2000s, including spots in World of Warcraft, El Tigre: The Adventures of Manny Rivera, Avatar: The Last Airbender, The Sims 2, Chowder, and Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel, just to name a few, but it wasn't long before he graduated to become the prolific actor he's known as today.
In the 2010s, Bauza took on parts in video games like Batman: Arkham City, Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, and Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy 13. Eventually, his work in animation took him to the Looney Tunes universe, where he would go on to play modern iterations on characters like Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian, and many, many others.
"I’m in complete shock and disbelief," Phineas and Ferb's Vincent Martella said. "A tremendously talented and kind coworker who I always had great conversations with and learned from. Sending so much love to his family. He was a giant. A titan in our industry."
More recently, pop-culture fans may have caught him voicing a few names in Invincible or The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. He also played characters in kids-programming-turned-horror-film Buddy, as well as High on Life 2. Moviegoers heard him reprise his role as Bugs Bunny and other classic Looney Tunes characters in the once-shelved Coyote vs. Acme when it made its way to theaters in August of this year. You can also hear him as Jin-Woo, Kuzon, Pich, and more in Avatar: Seven Havens.
For all intents and purposes, Bauza was a legend not just in animation but entertainment in general. You could fill a book just listing the roles he's played, and that's exactly why the internet has already lit up with friends, fans, and fellow entertainers posting their condolences. IGN interviewed Bauza about how he fought to save Coyote vs. Acme in 2024. You can see some of the ways the internet is remembering the star below.

He had the warmest smile and was always sincere. He let his talent speak for itself and made everyone feel like he was their biggest fan. He will always be a legend but I'm devastated that I'll never be able to give him a hug, or hear him joke, or see him smile again. Fuck, man.

item.title: Bandai Namco has revealed a 10th anniversary update for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 as fans await the fighting game series' third installment.
item.description:
Bandai Namco has revealed a 10th anniversary update for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 as fans await the fighting game series' third installment.
The publisher detailed the contents set to drop in the coming days on its website. Split between two major releases – one October 27, the other October 30 – all the new goodies will be available for anyone who has picked up Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 on PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, or Xbox Series X/S since it first launched October 25, 2016.
The first free update is said to bring login bonus rewards, special costumes, and an update for the Future Saga Chapter 4 DLC's Gallery of Time when it launches Tuesday. A true birthday celebration, called "Final Festival of Universes," will follow with hard-to-find items, as well as unlocks for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 rewards, come Friday.
"During the Final Festival of Universes, you will be able to raise your camaraderie level with characters who have accompanied you on your journey, choosing between Trunks, The Supreme Kai of Time, or Fu," according to an official description. "Doing so will unlock special illustrations. In addition, hard-to-obtain items will be coming back, and you will be able to earn 25 times more Star Coins than usual, making it easier than ever to exchange them for rewards."
Today marks 10 years since Bandai Namco launched its Dragon Ball action RPG follow-up. The Final Festival of Universes seems to be the publisher's sendoff for the sequel, which makes sense considering there's another game right around the corner.
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 was re-revealed for PC and consoles in April of this year and promised to drop players into West City in Age 1000. In an official description shared at the time, Bandai Namco said, "The game combines an epic story-driven RPG experience that will take DRAGON BALL fans on an unforgettable, action-packed journey into this new universe and its cast of characters."
Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 Screenshots
Fans were hoping the 10-year wait for a third installment wouldn't be too much longer when Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 was first revealed with its broad 2027 release date. Unfortunately, following narrowed release plans shared earlier this month, it's looking like we'll have to wait another year to go hands-on. When updates will arrive before then is unclear, with producer Masayuki Hirano attributing the slight push back to a desire to "fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward."
The Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 festivities should help the more impatient fans for at least a little while longer. In the meantime, you can read IGN's original 7.5/10 review for the sequel, where we called it "an ambitious, if rough-edged experience, with deceptively deep RPG and brawling elements."

item.title: The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.
item.description:
The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.
It's been a whirlwind week for Mass Effect players and fans of the now-shuttered legendary RPG developer BioWare. After EA announced it would be closing the studio and canceling development for Mass Effect 5, fans took action, and the result is something to behold.
In the first weekend of the #SaveMassEffect movement and its accompanying petition, more than 200,000 verified users have offered their signature to the cause. That's thanks in part to the wild amount of social media attention it's garnered in just a few days, but two of its most prominent supporters have already been backing Mass Effect for decades.
I like this thought…❤️💙#MassEffect #Femshep #broshep #N7 https://t.co/wnCS1I1w0u
"You know what I like to think about?" actor Jennifer Hale, who famously played the female version of Commander Shepard for the first three Mass Effect games, said in a video over the weekend. "I like to think about a world where the fans come together to create a Kickstarter, and then a couple of investors join them, and then a really cool game company joins them. Then a collective is formed to bring Mass Effect back to life for the community, for the creatives – for all of us – and it's amazing. That's what I like to think about."
It's a scenario that fans have pushed for, and one Hale believes in. She had already spoken out about the sadness surrounding BioWare's closure after a leaked trailer for its canceled Mass Effect: Universe project found its way online. At the time, she felt "weirdly hopeful," and just a few days later, she donned the #SaveMassEffect hashtag in a post.
When Hale first shared her feelings about EA's decision to lay off staff and bring the game side of the franchise to a halt, she wasn't alone. Joining her during an Instagram livestream was male Shepard actor Mark Meer. He echoed her thoughts, saying that it was "very sad news" for BioWare's home location in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and the industry as a whole. He returned to social media to share a similar video, #SaveMassEffect in tow.
I like it too. Hold the line.#MassEffect #SaveMassEffect #N7 #MassEffectIsAlive #CommanderShepard https://t.co/vx22yejYbR
"I just saw my friend, Jennifer Hale, post about an idea, and I think it's a pretty good one," Meer said. "Save Mass Effect. Hold the line. I should go, and you should go… sign that petition."
At the time of this story's publication, the #SaveMassEffect petition on Change.org, which aims to "prominently illustrate to EA the significance of this iconic series" and demand it continue, has crossed the 200,000-signature mark. It's thanks in part to the continued signal boosting from notable figures like Hale and Meer, who may not have even been included in new Mass Effect games, but they aren't the only ones without a stake in the franchise's future who chose to speak up.
Destiny players, who did their own fair share of organizing when Sony moved to cease development of Destiny 2 content earlier this year, have been a vocal force in the aftermath of BioWare's closure. Although it's hard to say whether organization of this magnitude might impact any decisions to give BioWare developers and their ideas a path forward, the effort is a bit heartwarming to see.
Others from different gaming communities have also done their best to lend a hand. You don't have to search too hard to find posts encouraging anyone who's ever had a brush with Shepard's fight against the Reapers to lend their signature to the cause. Another significant helping hand arrived from developer Owlcat Games, which used the official X/Twitter account for its upcoming game, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, to ask followers to consider signing the petition in a currently pinned post.
#SaveMassEffect https://t.co/6J8yg2dfCQ
The Expanse show was saved by fans in the past. So the #SaveMassEffect movement has our full support.Please consider signing the petition (link in the quoted post).
Don’t forget, Guardians. We share a bond with Mass Effect. Do your part.#SaveMassEffect https://t.co/EKq0hjssTx
Last month, Destiny players were shocked to hear that Bungie was revisiting its plans for the franchise after its community spoke up. In general, revivals at this level are unlikely, and there's no telling if Mass Effect fans will be quite as lucky, but for now, fans don't seem to show any sign of stopping. While we wait to see what is, hopefully, next for the legendary sci-fi RPG series, you can learn more about Mass Effect: Universe thanks to some recently leaked gameplay details. You can also read about the fans hoping to organize a boycott against EA. And for a trip down memory lane, our own Xbox guru Ryan McCaffrey shared his memories of the original Mass Effect and its powerful story in celebration of Xbox's imminent 25th anniversary.

item.title: Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos.
item.description:
Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos.
The Marvel Cinematic Universe newcomer tried his best not to play coy during a conversation with Rolling Stone. When pressed on whether comic book fans will see his shaved head fighting against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom at any point in the next year or so, he insisted he doesn't have any additional team-up movies on his plate for now.
"I don't think so," when asked if he'll appear in any cameo roles before X-Men. "I don't even know… See, what's happening? What do you mean?"
Christopher Abbott, who will play Professor X in 2028's ‘X-Men’ reboot, says he will not be in the upcoming Avengers movie.“I don't think so. Well, I don't even know–what's happening? What do you mean? I don't know what's going on. On no. I'm not in that. I gotta do the ‘X-Men’ movie first before any of that stuff.”
When the interviewer clarified, asking if he'll play in Doomsday, he had a quick reply: "No, I'm not in that."
Abbott joined a cast of other would-be mutant heroes when Marvel Studios confirmed he had been picked to play Professor X at D23 earlier this year. The announcement also came with a May 2028 release date, giving him plenty of time to prepare to play the group's leader, and if fans are lucky, show up for a scene or two beforehand.
After all, Doomsday and Secret Wars aren't just your run-of-the-mill superhero flicks. These are saga-ending event films packed to the gills with A-listers and, of course, cameos to keep the MCU going well into the future. With the 2000s versions of the X-Men, including Patrick Stewart's version of Charles Xavier, having already shown up for a few Doomsday trailers, many have wondered if the new X-Men cast would show up on-screen before Marvel's 2027 slate launched. If Abbott is out, though, the chances of an early MCU debut for other X-Men (besides Sadie Sink's Jean Grey) just got a little less likely.
"I gotta do the X-Men movie first before any of that stuff," he continued.
MCU X-Men Cast as of D23 2026
When the interviewer interjected, pointing out that hard launching characters without a cameo is "famously not how Marvel works," Abbott said with a chuckle, "Look, no coyness: I'm not in that movie."
With Doomsday less than two months from its December 18, 2026, release date, it really does sound like Abbott won't show up. However, his answer regarding Secret Wars, the only other movie between now and X-Men, didn't seem quite as definitive. With more than a full year before that film follows come December 17, 2027, and no trailers out yet, who knows? That said, at least as far as this new take on Professor X is concerned, it is still probably best not to get hopes up too high in the meantime.
Set to join Abbott on the team are Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Asa Germann as Angel, and more. We'll at least see the X-Men team unite when the reboot premieres May 5, 2028. Until then, you can get a sneak peek at Navarrette's progress on developing Rogue's accent.

item.title: Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.
item.description:
Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.
It's a strong start for the low-budget DCU film, split between $24 million domestically and $19 million internationally. The opening weekend total falls toward the higher end of early projections as audiences showed up to see Tom Rhys Harries bring a twisted and often overlooked Batman villain to the big screen.
With brutal body horror elements in a story that sees the birth of its titular character, Clayface follows Matt Hagen as he attempts to rebuild his life after a horrible attack leaves his face scarred. Starring Harries, directed by James Watkins, and written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, this latest DCU movie took viewers into the darkest corners of James Gunn and Peter Safran's universe they've seen yet, with a pretty hard-R rating.
It's for these reasons that the DCU's foray into a new live-action Gotham City left fans with question marks as they feared how a more adult-oriented story could fit into the same world as something as bubbly and bright as 2025's Superman. So far, at least, it seems to have paid off, at least compared to Supergirl, which landed as a dud in the DCU earlier this year.
The Milly Alcock-led superhero movie was deemed a box office bomb after it premiered in June. That's mostly due to its almost $200 million budget, which towered over the comparatively measly $126.46 million it gathered throughout its run (via Box Office Mojo). Clayface, on the other hand, is starting its time in theaters almost matching the $44 million budget reported by Variety.
Although there is certainly plenty of ground to cover before officially being declared a success, it seems like a strong start. A few factors will help carry Clayface throughout the rest of its run: Firstly, its October release timing means Halloween moviegoers will have something spooky to watch next weekend. Reviews have been pretty solid, too, with Rotten Tomatoes recording a 75% from critics and 94% from audiences.

item.title: Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.
item.description:
Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.
The long-awaited and currently canned follow-up for the sci-fi RPG franchise, which was working under the title Mass Effect: Universe, was built around decisions made in the original games, according to comments shared by former technical director Romain Toutain during a recent livestream (via Kotaku). As more details about the project leak, there's no telling exactly how thorough this system would have been, but he did his best to give fans an idea.
"All the choices made in the first Mass Effect games were taken into account," Toutain said (translation via Bluesky user @loustica-lucia.bsky.social). "One of the reasons why it was called 'Mass Effect: Universe' is that you had so many choices. That you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes, to keep it simple. It's not exactly how it worked. You had different timelines, basically."
Every IGN Mass Effect Review
Mass Effect fans know how crucial the series' overarching story is, especially when it comes to Commander Shepard's first three installments in his/her fight against the Reapers. Outside of the ill-fated Andromeda follow-up that launched in 2017, players were able to carry major choices from each entry over to the next, resulting in a trilogy of games with a highly personalized story.
Relationships, major character deaths, and even the fate of an entire species are just a few of the ways Shepard can be steered to shape the galaxy, and although whether it was all worth it in the end is still up for debate, it seems Mass Effect: Universe would have offered an opportunity to right some wrongs. Toutain said they had plans for those who just prefer to experiment with the story and its many, many branches, too. He likened the freedom to "generate timelines" to Spike Chunsoft's 2016 video game, Zero Time Dilemma.
"You have no f**king idea just how great it was," he continued. Then, responding to a fan asking whether Mass Effect: Universe would have featured systems similar to what was found in Dragon Age: Inquisition and the series' lore-tailoring Keep application, he said, "kinda, yeah."
Did you play through the entire Mass Effect Trilogy? If so, which was your favorite?

item.title: Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6, has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.
item.description:
Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6, has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.
Rockstar Games has refrained from confirming the vast majority of the cast of next month's new GTA game, but as if there was ever any doubt, that hasn't stopped ravenous fans from piecing a list together themselves. Perez is one name theorists have talked about for years, so she took a few minutes to let thousands of viewers get to know her while masterfully dodging a swarm of GTA 6 comments along the way.
Reaching a peak of more than 2,100 viewers on a six-month-old Instagram account with just nine posts, Perez spent her 12-minute livestream just talking about her life growing up in a "small, rural, redneck-y" town. She lives in a studio apartment with a dog, loves to cook, grew up driving trucks, and as far as everyone else is officially concerned, she definitely will not be the star of the so-called biggest video game of all time in a little less than a month.
"But yeah, no, I'm not rich. I'm a regular person," Perez said when responding to fans who assumed she was wealthy. "I live in a small studio apartment, which I love. I have my tiny, little itty-bitty kitchen, and it's just me and my dog. I do everything on my own, and I've done everything on my own for a very long time, and I love it, and I'm very grateful. I have a family that loves me, and I'm just feeling like I'm in a really good place, where I am in my life."
"I want a green truck," she said with a smile while ignoring the horde comments mentioning "Lucia" and "GTA 6." Some responded that, no, actually, she doesn't live alone, because she has Jason to keep her company. Others were subtler, asking if she'll be playing Rockstar's latest or if she's just "ready for next month." Despite the steady flow of responses begging her to confirm her alleged role – which would be guarded under a strict non-disclosure agreement, even if it were real – Perez only acknowledged users commenting about anything else.
Keep in mind that this all comes from years of clues gathered by fans, but Rockstar's lack of confirmation doesn't mean there's nothing to suggest Perez is playing Lucia in GTA 6. As others have highlighted, the actress has a history of live-action and voice roles. She has credits for single episodes of shows like Jessica Jones, The Blacklist, and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. Funnily enough, she also played a blackjack dealer in Grand Theft Auto Online.
Her place in Rockstar history may be given a bump when GTA 6 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S next month, November 19. If you're wondering who might be playing Lucia's partner in crime, Jason, fans have long speculated that Modern Family and Grey's Anatomy actor Dylan Rourke filled the role, but he, too, has yet to be confirmed.
Who has been confirmed, whether Rockstar and any likely NDAs like it or not, is Stephen Root, who said he will be seen playing drug trafficker Brian Heder. Otherwise, we might need to wait until launch to see the full cast, so don't go sending messages to any actors just yet.
Fans may have tracked down the voice actors behind one of the biggest game launches of all time, but it's par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto players. One fan spent three months charting planetary positions just to try and learn when trailer 3 would premiere (they were wrong). Another fan measured oxygen levels to try and achieve the same feat (they, too, were wrong).
Either way, GTA 6 marketing is continuing to ramp up. While we wait these last few precious weeks, you can see why some fans are expecting a sweep at The Game Awards 2026. You can also learn more about the love and care Rockstar put into its new video game, but don't forget to read up on IGN's interview.

item.title: A knife-wielding man was arrested Friday night for threatening crew members on the Brooklyn set of Miami Vice ‘85. Citing information from the NYPD, TMZ reports that a police officer working security on the set arrested Alex Perez, 23.
item.description:
A knife-wielding man was arrested Friday night for threatening crew members on the Brooklyn set of Miami Vice ‘85.
Citing information from the NYPD, TMZ reports that a police officer working security on the set arrested Alex Perez, 23.
“Perez can be seen being escorted off the set by a staffer before taking out the large knife from his sweatshirt pocket,” according to TMZ, which also posted a video of the incident.
“A cop on the scene then arrested Perez — who hurled the n-word at the production staff member while in cuffs — at 11:17 PM.”
The site reports that Perez has been charged with menacing with a weapon in the 2nd degree and criminal possession of a weapon in the 4th degree.
Miami Vice ‘85 has been filming in New York this week, including scenes featuring Michael B. Jordan and John Leguizamo in that appear to faithfully recreate the opening moments of the original TV series’ pilot.
Director Joseph Kosinski’s film is inspired by the series’ two-part pilot (“Brother’s Keeper”) and the show’s first season in general.
For more on Miami Vice ‘85, check out these first look images of Jordan and Austin Butler in costume as detectives Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively.
Miami Vice ‘85 will relocate production to Miami, Florida after hurricane season is over. The film opens in theaters on May 19, 2028.

item.title: DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers.
item.description:
DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers.
Clayface poured into the DCU when it brought the tragic story of Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries) to theaters yesterday. A bloody body horror movie with a firm R rating, its October release date makes sense as it molded its way into the comic book movie universe with a more adult story, but not everyone is happy with the film's place in the universe.
Despite solid scores from critics and fans (IGN gave it a 7/10 review), there are DC watchers who have continued to complain that executives like Gunn and co-chairman Peter Safran haven't done a good job of using smaller stories to build toward bigger tie-in projects. For reference, the DCU technically started with animated series Creature Commandos before heading to theaters with Superman. Peacemaker Season 2, Supergirl, Lanterns, and Clayface then followed.
While standalone Wonder Woman and Batman movies are in the cards, projects like The People v. Gorilla Grodd seem to be further along than most, with crossover moments mostly limited so far. So, what gives? Gunn has an easy answer that might leave impatient fans wanting more, but for him, it's a solution that will keep the DCU telling quality stories for years to come.
"I couldn't agree more," he said when replying to a fan defending the cinematic universe on Threads. "DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren't meaningful unless they lead to something else."
Gunn continued, saying it's "strange" to see "people not understanding this" considering Star Wars has taken a similar approach for decades. He did admit Disney's sci-fi franchise may not have the "tonal variety" of something like the DCU, which has so far ping-ponged between serious drama and action to comedy and, most recently, horror. Still, he wants fans to know that, no matter how different each movie or show may be, there is still connective tissue holding them together.
Which new DCU project are you most excited for?

item.title: Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war."
item.description:
Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war."
The filmmaker behind Skydance-Paramount's upcoming reimagining of Activision's massive first-person shooter series dived into his thoughts on the franchise during an interview with ComicBook. We already know the Call of Duty movie will focus on the Modern Warfare portion of the FPS universe, and it sounds like Berg and writer Taylor Sheridan have already looked to the games it's based on for inspiration.
"So Modern Warfare, if you really look at the missions, and the storylines, and the characters – like Captain Price, and Soap, and Ghost, and Alex – these are complicated humans," Berg said. "These are not – and no disrespect – cartoon characters or comic books. These are very nuanced storylines; like, there's a real soul to the Modern Warfare universe…
The Best Video Game Movies of All Time
"And, yes, there's violence, and there's hardware, and equipment, and there's killing – but underneath it I think the game, and the craters of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry."
Berg seems to be putting in the work to nail a Modern Warfare story for the big screen, but not every fan is convinced that he's the right guy for the job. That's mostly because he had some not-so-nice things to say about gaming back in 2013. When asked for his take on video games based on war at the time, he said, called them "pathetic," using the term, "keyboard courage."
"I think anyone that sits around playing video games for four hours... It's weak," Berg elaborated at the time. "Get out, do something."
These days he's changed his tune, and judging by his affection for characters like Captain Price and Ghost, he's hoping to do right by Modern Warfare and its fans. His upcoming film, The Mosquito Bowl, is a sports-war film set to premiere later this month. His vision for the Call of Duty movie will start to take shape after that.
